baer-heitev/1:ב: (2) Needle. It is difficult — for perhaps there will be a mefulesh hole in it, and it is invalid per the Rosh and Tur, and likewise in Shulchan Aruch seif 2 per the first view — one can say that mefulesh disqualifies only when pierced from this side to the opposite side facing it, or to the seed chambers; but if the hole on one side is mefulesh, that is, through its thickness, certainly all agree it does not disqualify without a deficiency, for we derive etrog laws from treifot of an animal, and in treifot if there is a mefulesh hole in the thickness of the limb such as in the heart or intestines and it does not reach the cavity, certainly there is no treifah; so too with etrog. Taz:
baer-heitev/7:ב: (2) Pitom. It is implied from his wording specifically that the entire thing was removed. But Beit Yosef, Bach, and Levush wrote to be stringent even if part of it was removed, and per Magen Avraham, and it appears to me in any case we require that it be removed up to the etrog, since the reason is because of a deficiency as written siman 649 seif 5 in the gloss — if so, if anything at all was removed it is not called deficient, for this is not a noticeable deficiency. And see Eliyah Rabbah:
baer-heitev/9:_: Mostly. From the anonymous wording it is implied that he holds "its majority" means from two sides, as the Tur wrote:
baer-heitev/12:א: (1) Chazazit. Like two boils at minimum, and they must be visible to the eye when one holds it in his hand. From Beit Yosef in Knesset HaGedolah:
beer-hagolah/1:ב: Tur in the name of the Raavad
beer-hagolah/4:ב: Tur in the name of "there are those who are stringent," and to this he agreed
beer-hagolah/5:א: Mishnah there 34 and in the Gemara 37, and as Rashi and Rosh explained
beur-hagra/1:א: (1) And the measure, etc. For here one cannot say from mixing, for once it dries it reddens; rather as written in the previous chapter — whatever is pierced, etc., and the moisture is to the fruit like blood is to flesh, and he did not write in the gloss like R' Yosef ben Meshulam as explained above siman 646 seif 7:
beur-hagra/3:א: (1) Seif 3 — mefulesh. There are those who say, etc. Like an open alleyway, and so in the Tosefta — even in a crack we require from side to side, for we recite there at the beginning of Ohalot, and the Rosh brought there chapter 3 mishnah 4: an etrog that was perforated and they plugged it with a reed — it is not a connection, for human connections are not connections, etc. An etrog that split into two is pure and one need not be concerned that something is missing. And the Rosh wrote: and it appears that it split not that it was completely divided but that it was joined, etc. And know that at the beginning it teaches "perforated and perforated," and here it teaches "split," and he wrote: and pure means kosher. And from here is proof for the latter view that seif 2 holds we require a deficiency, for splitting is no worse than piercing, and this is what "and one need not be concerned" means, etc. And this is because we also consider a crack:
beur-hagra/5:ב: (2) And there are those who say, etc. For all disqualifications in its pitom — all the more so like chazazit. And the first view holds that when we disqualify in its pitom all the more so, specifically those disqualifications that disqualify in its majority, like chazazit, as written in the Yerushalmi — its pitom is like its majority for disqualification:
beur-hagra/12:ב: (2) And there are those who say, etc. For the reason that in its pitom it disqualifies all the more so is because the hadar of the etrog is there, and dry is also invalid because of hadar as written there; and see Rosh seif 20. And Magen Avraham in Tosafos Shulchan Aruch — the first view disagrees regarding dry, and it seems to him that we do not disqualify in its pitom except those that disqualify in its majority as above; and even though a lung that dried even partially is treifah, that is when it peeled in the fingernail area, but shriveled specifically in its entirety — and b'dieved siman 36 seif 13 and seif 14:
beur-hagra/13:ב: (2) And there are those who say, etc. As the Rosh wrote — chazazit is invalid because it does not show the appearance of an etrog, and therefore peeled is kosher even in its majority, since it shows the appearance of an etrog even though their appearances are not equal; and see siman 17, and these since they are common they show the appearance of an etrog:
beur-hagra/21:_: Seif 21 — unless it returns, etc. As explained above 31:2 — because the fruit did not finish ripening, not because of hadar; and since it returns to its appearance, therefore the fruit finished ripening:
biur-halacha/9:א: In two or in three places — the Kesef Mishnah asked: now "two three" should be required; and the Taz answered that this is what it means: it compares three to two, that is, even with two we require that they spread one from the other at least enough for the measure of a third chazazit (that is, enough for the measure of two small boils and showing etrog appearance somewhat — like a hair's breadth stops between this chazazit and the chazazit next to it must be so, and likewise from the other side); but with less than this it is not called speckled. And many of the later authorities rejected his answer — who knows how much is the measure of the boils that we measure by this the gap between two chazazit? And they answered that in such a case the Gemara asks in chapter Mefanin and they answered as people say; see Peri Megadim and Gedei Yeshua and Nehar Shalom. Nevertheless, the essence of his view that he wrote it is reasonable that by a hair's breadth showing etrog appearance that stops between chazazit and chazazit it does not appear speckled — it appears correct for practical halacha:
biur-halacha/14:_: If when one peels it, etc., it is kosher — see Mishna Berurah that even l'chatchila it is permitted; and Peri Megadim wrote that nevertheless on Yom Tov it is forbidden to peel it and make it kosher, for it is fixing, like it is forbidden to pick hadas grapes on Yom Tov:
biur-halacha/16:_: If it is black or white — and see Chayei Adam who wrote that red is from the appearance of an etrog. And the view of Peri Megadim is that red in redness is an invalid appearance, but like a pink hue one can say it is a kosher appearance:
biur-halacha/21:_: That it resembles, etc. — see in Mishna Berurah what we wrote regarding grafted etrogs, and this is the language of Bikkurei Yaakov: it is simple that the etrogs that grow among us in Ashkenaz lands in the gardens of nobles are all grafted; but those that come from Italy and are possibly grafted would apparently be kosher if we cannot determine — we follow the majority, and the majority of etrogs in the world are known not to be grafted; thus for practical halacha requires further study; and in any case if there is doubt of grafting, if he has no other he should take it without a blessing, end of his words. And in my humble opinion one can say that for this reason several poskim relied on signs even though there is not so much proof as the later poskim wrote, because with combination of majority one may rely on this; and therefore one should not protest one who relies on this and recites a blessing, as seems to me:
chokhmat-shlomo/3:_: (There, seif 11) If it is half-and-half in one place, etc. Note: see in Taz that there is a difficulty in the Mishnah's precise wording against itself — at first it states on its majority invalid, which implies that with a minority it is kosher, and afterward it states on its minority kosher, which implies that with a minority it is invalid; see there. And in my humble opinion it would seem to reconcile: that a deficiency is kosher on the other days, and there are differences of opinion below per the Ran brought in the gloss below — it is proven that he holds specifically that its majority must remain intact, then it is kosher, and not when only a minority remains; and from the words of Maharai that Magen Avraham brought it is implied that he holds even if only its minority remains intact it is kosher. And in my humble opinion it would seem to decide that if its majority was removed and only its minority remains such — it is invalid per the Ran, for in this case his reason applies well — it is not called an etrog but pieces of etrog; that is, since its majority was removed and only its minority remains, therefore it is called only a piece of etrog and therefore invalid; but if half remained, since in any case its majority was not removed, it is not called a piece of an etrog since the majority was not removed — in this law with Maharai it is kosher. Therefore one can say there is a difference between the first day of Yom Tov and the other days: on the other days we require specifically that it be on its majority; but with a minority, even if chazazit disqualifies even in a minority, nevertheless it is kosher because it is no worse than removal and is considered in any case as if it does not exist; and since if it had been removed from the etrog it would be kosher even though it was not yet removed, it is kosher because whatever is in his hand is not like something lacking an action, as the poskim wrote regarding a Torah scroll on Shabbos — if it is in his hand to fix it, it is kosher; so too here. But on the first day of Yom Tov, if deficient it is invalid, then necessarily if we judge it as it is now, even with a minority it is not hadar; and if we judge it as if removed, behold again it is deficient and invalid; therefore it is kosher only in its minority, for then there is no chazazit on it. Therefore the Mishnah states the decided matter: one who has chazazit on its majority — invalid even on the second day of Yom Tov, for in this case it is necessarily as above; and one who has it on its minority — kosher even on the first day of Yom Tov, unlike with a minority there is a difference — on the first day of Yom Tov invalid and on the second day kosher. And if so, the implication of the poskim does not seem to show this difference; nevertheless the reasoning supports as written. And further it would seem to say: since etrog laws are compared to treifot, as written in the Gemara and Tosafos daf 36 — if so one can say so too here: since in treifot with two adverse factors it is treifah, so too with etrog; therefore one who has chazazit on its majority is invalid even without joining another adverse factor; but on its minority it is kosher if there is no other adverse factor; but if there is another adverse factor it is invalid even combined with a minority of chazazit; therefore at first it states one who has chazazit on its majority — invalid even without another adverse factor, and afterward it states if chazazit rose on its minority — kosher even though there is still another adverse factor that its pitom was removed, even combined with all these adverse factors it is kosher; but with a minority, if there is no other adverse factor it is kosher, but with another adverse factor it is invalid. And behold Tosafos wrote in this sugya daf 35b s.v. "if chazazit rose on its majority" — in the Yerushalmi it is somewhat implied that only on the first day of Yom Tov it disqualifies, as I explained in the previous chapter. And behold I wonder regarding what they brought this Yerushalmi, since in our Gemara it is implied the opposite from what it asks — on the contrary, in two and three places it appears speckled and invalid, and it concludes that it refers to the latter clause, etc.; and it is difficult, since in the end one must emend and reverse the version from kosher to invalid — why need to answer that it refers to the latter clause? It should have remained as at first that it refers to the first clause, only that the intent is thus: since the Mishnah states specifically chazazit together with piercing and deficiency all the more so, therefore it is implied it is invalid only on the first day of Yom Tov, similar to piercing, as Tosafos wrote at the end of the chapter; therefore it says well "if in one place" — only with a minority then it is not invalid except on the first day of Yom Tov and on the second day kosher; but in two and three places it would be speckled and invalid even on the second day of Yom Tov, for from the language of the Gemara it is proven that in two and three places it is worse than one place on its majority, as it asks in the language "on the contrary" — if so it should answer thus that in two and three places it is invalid even on the second day of Yom Tov; and since it does not answer thus, it is proven that it is obvious to him that chazazit on its majority is invalid all seven days; and if so, why did they bring the words of the Yerushalmi here? Requires further study. And behold per the above it would seem to explain the language of the Yerushalmi that R' Yehuda says in the name of R' Shmuel: all disqualifications do not disqualify except on the first day of Yom Tov alone. There they say: and its majority from one side, etc. And behold at first glance from his words in two and three places it is better and it is kosher, and in our Gemara it is implied the opposite; and see Shirrei Korban who addressed this, and in his explanation there it was forced to reconcile. And per what I wrote one can say this follows the view: since all disqualifications do not disqualify except on the first day of Yom Tov, but on the second day kosher even for chazazit; therefore it says well that on its majority from one side it is that which is not invalid except on the first day of Yom Tov, but in two and three places invalid even on the second day of Yom Tov, for it is like speckled; and one can say, and it is correct. And I saw in the Rosh that he brought this Yerushalmi and explains explicitly the above view; and why did he not explain further that the intent is that even on the second day of Yom Tov it is invalid in two and three places? And I saw there that he disagrees with the Yerushalmi from reasoning — and the matter is puzzling why he does not prove more from the Gemara that necessarily he does not hold thus, since he does not explain the words of R' Chananel thus; requires further study:
chokhmat-shlomo/4:_: (There, seif 12) It disqualifies chazazit and any change of appearance all the more so, etc. Note: Here I saw in Shaarei Teshuvah of the Gaon Moharaz zatzal in this siman in the name of responsa Penei Aryeh that tends to permit red appearance. And in my opinion, God forbid, to say thus; for it is true that from the language of Shulchan Aruch in seif 16 that he wrote in his wording "if it is black or white" and did not mention red — it is implied red is kosher; but this is not a single proof, for one can say he wrote thus to include that even in black or white if it is not on its majority it is kosher, and all the more so red. But if it is on its majority or on its pitom all the more so, invalid even if red; and even if one says specifically black or white and not red — nevertheless it appears that this is specifically below, like there we rule that it disqualifies only on its majority or in three places; so too we rule red is kosher in it; but above its pitom, which disqualifies in it all the more so, red also disqualifies. And proof from the language of Shulchan Aruch seif 12 that he wrote in his wording that any change of appearance disqualifies in it. From this language it is implied that any change of appearance disqualifies anything that is not the appearance of an etrog. And perhaps Penei Aryeh also concedes in this that above its pitom it disqualifies. And what Penei Aryeh wrote that in an apple red is common — what is this proof to an etrog? Because it is called an apple should its appearance be kosher? Behold an apple's way is to be green, and for several views invalid on an etrog; and also we see that in white and black, if it is in two and three places it is invalid even though a small amount of it does not disqualify — nevertheless in three places it appears speckled and invalid. If so, so too above its pitom, if it is not like the appearance of lightning to be on an etrog, invalid, for it is like speckled and invalid. And behold in a Torah scroll, even per the view that passing a quill over the Name helps, nevertheless in several names it is invalid because it is like speckled even though the writing independently is the way to be in a Torah scroll; nevertheless if it is not equal to the rest of the writing it is like speckled; so too on an etrog above its pitom, any appearance that is not the way of an etrog to be thus, it is like speckled and invalid. And likewise below from the slope in three places it appears invalid for reason of speckled, not per the view of Penei Aryeh; and so we practice, and our intent is for the sake of Heaven and may it be acceptable before Him, amen. And behold in law: if one robbed from him a good etrog, whether it suffices to return to him an inferior etrog — see in my compositions Bava Kamma chapter Merubah (Bava Kamma daf 78), see there with God's help what I wrote to reconcile the words of Maharam Mintz, see there. And behold in law: if at first it was a beautiful etrog and afterward some change of appearance arose in it due to handling and the like — whether it is disqualified from this or not. Behold as I think I already wrote on this matter and forgot its place. And behold it appears at first glance proof from Rashi in Sukkah daf 31b s.v. "since Rava [said] etrog in the right hand," etc. — if so it is too large, perhaps it will fall from his hand and become disqualified that a hole will occur in it, end of his words. And it is difficult why he states specifically a hole — he should have said there will be a change of appearance in it because it will get dirty and there will be a change of appearance. And in my opinion it is easier for an etrog to have a change of appearance than a hole, and a hole does not disqualify except like an issur-size hole, and a change of appearance disqualifies all the more so; and in any case he should have stated both — a hole or a change of appearance. And necessarily it appears that Rashi holds a change of appearance disqualifies only if it comes from itself, but due to something else it does not disqualify, and specifically through something else, since it is possible to rinse and remove it, it does not disqualify. However, there is room to reject — for behold still this is difficult, he should have stated that its pitom or its stem will be removed. Therefore it appears that Rashi holds the concern is not for disqualification alone — what of it if nothing prohibited will result from it; rather the main concern is that it will become disqualified and he will not know of this and go out with it and be nullified from the mitzvah and recite a blessing in vain; therefore Rashi holds this is only out of concern for a hole, for in this, since we require issur-size measure, perhaps he will imagine there is not issur-size in it and err to declare it kosher and come to prohibition and nullification of mitzvah; but where there is no concern of error and disqualification is obvious and there is no concern of error for this, no need "it will fall and become disqualified." Therefore Rashi explained a hole, and there is no proof here for this law; examine, and see in my compositions Orach Chayyim year 5601 siman 649 in responsa to the community of Odessa to Rabbi Moshe Ze'ev may he live, see there, and examine:
eliyah-rabbah/3:_: [3] And certainly dry, etc. It is implied that examination with a needle does not help, and so ruled Bach, not like Taz; and if they buried it in honey the moisture is sustained and examination helps (Bach), and Taz disagrees for it is like pickled as he wrote in Taz, and perhaps it is reasonable to Bach that we do not say pickled in water except regarding prohibition:
eliyah-rabbah/10:_: [10] [Levush] And it is that which did not change, etc. Explanation: in appearance, like a place that was not peeled; and per the Tur who ruled like the Raavad. But Bach expanded that even the Raavad did not forbid where it lacks etrog appearance except in two and three places; but in one place, even on its majority or on its pitom, kosher as long as it is not an invalid appearance, and so he ruled. And I add that even in two and three places it is fit to declare kosher as long as it is not an invalid appearance, for I found in Sefer Tamim De'im siman 130 that the Raavad himself agrees with "there are those who say" that specifically with invalid appearance we require; see there. And in any case on its pitom it seems to me to disqualify, for as I wrote above per the Raavad — even where it has etrog appearance, peeled on the pitom area is also called etrog disqualification; if so, certainly it is fit to be stringent where it lacks etrog appearance:
kaf-hachayyim/2:_: 2) There. A dry etrog is invalid. Disqualification of dryness on an etrog disqualifies only on its majority, like lulav and hadas, for we do not disqualify in them except on the majority of leaves. But if the dryness is on its pitom, the Rosh and Ran wrote that just as chazazit disqualifies on its pitom in any amount, so too the law with dryness, and all disqualifications that disqualify on an etrog are because of hadar. From Mateh Yehuda part 2 in Likutim to Shulchan Aruch daf 62b. Beit HaShoevah letter 5, and see below seif 12 and in our words there b'siyata diShmaya:
kaf-hachayyim/4:_: 4) There. And he shall examine by passing a needle through it, etc. And it is difficult — for perhaps there will be a mefulesh hole in it, and it is invalid per the Rosh and Tur, and likewise in Shulchan Aruch in seif 2 per the first view; and one can say that mefulesh does not disqualify except when pierced from this side to the opposite side facing it or to the seed chambers; but if the hole on one side is mefulesh, that is, through its thickness, certainly all agree it does not disqualify without deficiency, for we derive etrog laws from treifot of an animal, and in treifot if there is a mefulesh hole in the thickness of the limb such as in the heart or intestines and it does not reach the cavity, certainly there is no treifah; so too here with etrog. Taz seif katan 1. However Machatzit HaShekel wrote to explain the words of Magen Avraham seif katan 1 — that even if one pierces only the thick peel from side to side it is called mefulesh; therefore one must turn the needle and not insert it in the needle-hole but insert the needle with thread on the side of the needle-hole and not pass the needle through to the other side, and again remove the needle with the thread on the same side and look at the thread whether there is moisture in it — if so there is no mefulesh hole; see there, and so too Eliyah Rabbah letter 1 and Levush. And one must be careful that the needle not enter the seed chambers. Eliyah Rabbah there. And in one made face-to-face (dafa dafa) and one of the protrusions was pierced — one can say for all it is kosher, for side-to-side mefulesh means through to the other side, not one protrusion alone. From Shulchan Aruch HaRav letter 1, Mishna Berurah in Shaarei HaTziyon letter 7 — and this is when there is no deficiency. Mishna Berurah there:
kaf-hachayyim/5:_: 5) There. And he shall examine by passing a needle through it, etc. This examination of the Rosh and Tur and Shulchan Aruch — it is almost impossible that it not make some deficiency in it and disqualify it. Therefore it is better to insert a needle in it slightly and remove it from the same side it was inserted; and if the hole returns and fills after removing the needle, it is moist, and if not, its moisture has already been consumed and it dried — like what is written in Yerushalmi at the end of chapter 2 of Shevi'it regarding gourds: if it was hardened in the seventh year, etc.; and this is a light matter, it does not cause deficiency in an etrog even slightly. From Mo'ach Korkev. From Machberet letter 1, main points of Darkei Moshe siman 33 letter 29. However Beit HaShoevah letter 4 wrote it is possible an etrog is different, for even if the hole does not fill, still not all the moisture has completely finished; see there. And the Raavad in Sefer Tadir siman 232 wrote: pass a needle through it, and if there is moisture in it, it immediately comes out through the hole; see there. And although it is almost impossible that nothing be lacking from the peel of the etrog through inserting the needle — one can say that since that slight amount goes to the sides due to the pressure of the needle or enters inward, it is not considered deficient, and similar to what is written below that one inserts a peg and it is not mefulesh like issur-size and is kosher; see there:
kaf-hachayyim/7:_: 7) in the gloss. And certainly it is dry and invalid. And an etrog that they bury in honey so that the moisture in it will be sustained — one may not rely on this to declare it kosher without examination with needle and thread. Bach. Knesset HaGedolah in Hagahat HaTur letter 4. However Taz seif katan 17 wrote it is invalid because of pickled, and so too Rabbi Zalman letter 25. Beit HaShoevah letter 6 and letter 67. Mishna Berurah letter 54. And in Krosno we do not say pickled is like cooked as written in Yoreh De'ah siman 104 regarding a mouse. Machatzit HaShekel seif katan 22. Mishna Berurah in Shaarei HaTziyon letter 61. And see more of this below seif 15 and in our words there b'siyata diShmaya:
kaf-hachayyim/8:_: 8) And if he took in his hand an etrog to bless on it and afterward they brought him a more beautiful etrog — he is not obligated to put it down and bless on the more beautiful one. Shulchan Aruch HaRav part 1 siman 37 and part 2 siman 40, and so agreed in responsa Yad Eliyahu siman 72. However in responsa Chacham Tzvi siman 45 he disagreed with the words of Shulchan Aruch HaRav mentioned and concluded the matter is clear that whether regarding etrog, Hanukkah candles, or any mitzvah in the world — one blesses on the beautiful and mehudar and fulfills with it, even though it came last; see there. However if he already began the blessing he should not put it down and take the other; and so too if it is on the first day and this unattractive one is his and he took it in his hand to bless, and meanwhile his friend came and wants to give him a more mehudar gift on condition to return — better to fulfill the mitzvah with his own. So wrote Shaarei Teshuvah below siman 643 letter 1; see there. And in my humble opinion it appears that on day one it is better to bless on one's own even though he has not yet taken it in hand to bless, as long as there is no concern of disqualification, only because of hiddur — for a person prefers to perform a mitzvah with his own property; and also lest the owner of the etrog does not give as a complete gift with all his heart. And afterward I saw that Mahari Betz wrote thus part 3 siman 49, and Eliyah Rabbah brought it below siman 649 letter 18; see there. And see below letter 87, and further see above siman 554 letter 39:
kaf-hachayyim/9:_: 9) [Seif 2] An etrog that was pierced with a mefulesh hole, etc. And if the thick peel was pierced from side to side it is called mefulesh for all. Magen Avraham seif katan 2. Eliyah Rabbah letter 6 part 1 general rule 151 letter 2, Beit HaShoevah letter 8, and see below letter 24:
kaf-hachayyim/10:_: 10) There. In any amount it is invalid. Even if nothing is missing. Tur. Levush. Rabbi Zalman letter 4, and such as pierced by a needle that did not lack anything from the etrog at all — nevertheless any amount mefulesh is invalid:
kaf-hachayyim/15:_: 15) There. And if anything is missing it is invalid. And specifically when missing from the body of the etrog; but if only the upper peel is missing, which is like a kind of scab on the etrog, it is kosher for all, as written below seif 6; see there, and so Mishna Berurah in Be'er Heitev:
kaf-hachayyim/17:_: 17) We recite: two disqualifications they are — pierced and not missing, or missing any amount and not pierced — as Maran ruled in the first view that he wrote anonymously, for such is his known view. And if pierced and there is no deficiency, even in time of need take it without blessing in our places where we accepted Maran's ruling; but in other places in time of need one may rely to take it and bless. Rabbi Maharai Navon in Sefer Get Mekusher daf 24a. From Machberet letter 2, Beit HaShoevah letter 13. And see below letter 20:
kaf-hachayyim/19:_: 19) in the gloss. However if he sees that the skin and flesh are not intact, etc. It is implied that if there is doubt in this whether the flesh is intact, we follow the lenient view, since the latter view which is the Raavad holds that even if certainly there is deficiency it is kosher as long as it is not mefulesh and the deficiency is not issur-size — we may well rely on it in doubt at the very least. And if there is doubt whether it reaches the seed chambers, it is also kosher since there is no deficiency at all, and per the Raavad kosher even if mefulesh as long as there is no deficiency at all. Taz seif katan 5. Eliyah Rabbah there. Rabbi Zalman letter 10 and letter 11. Chayei Adam there. Mishna Berurah letter 11. And see Beit HaShoevah letter 12 who wrote this is specifically in places that follow the rulings of Maharil and rely on the latter view and declare kosher even if certainly there is deficiency per the Raavad; but other places that accepted Maran Shulchan Aruch's ruling disqualify even in time of need if there is deficiency in it, per the anonymous first view — if so, also if pierced on the tree in the way of its growth and we have doubt whether the flesh is intact, we disqualify it out of doubt; and even though it is a double doubt that turns — permitted even in certainty — nevertheless regarding blessing one should not bless, since blessings do not impede; see there. However it appears that what he wrote this is specifically in places, etc., is not necessary, for Taz returns on the words of Maharil zatzal, and the words of Maharil are on the first view; and also what he wrote one should not bless, etc. — we already wrote in several places that where there is a custom we do not say stam kula. And see below letter 26:
levushei-serad/3:_: There — except due to dryness, etc. It is dry and called shriveled because it is only in part of it, and Shulchan Aruch HaGedolah holds partial dryness is kosher, and we do not rule thus, as Magen Avraham wrote seif katan 17; therefore the Gra disqualified it; and in any case he brings proof from Shulchan Aruch HaGedolah that partial dryness is called shriveled, and in that case alone the Gra disqualified it; and he concludes one can say that although shriveled is kosher specifically in part of it, and like a healthy animal — dryness disqualifies in any amount, and shriveled that is here disqualifies specifically in its entirety:
machatzit-hashekel/1:א: Magen Avraham wrote: even shriveled, etc., and in Hagahot HaGra, etc., if he cut, etc. — Rama brought below siman 649 seif 5:
machatzit-hashekel/6:א: (Seif katan 6) If cracked on its majority, etc. And he was not precise, for specifically, etc., for this law derives from the Ran. And these are his words: per the version of Rabbi Yitzchak and Bach — there is one who explained it at length on its majority from two sides; however specifically below, but on its pitom even all the more so invalid, etc. And there are those stringent to disqualify even all the more so a crack from one side until its cavity, or even if it does not reach its cavity — as long as most of the thick outer peel is cracked, end of Ran's words; and Bach wrote that there are stringent ones in Ran that suffice with a crack from one side. Nevertheless it is invalid only when completely cracked. And nevertheless he calls them stringent in Ran, for nevertheless they are more stringent than one view that requires majority of two sides, for majority of two sides is a greater measure than an entire crack of one side. But if cracked on majority of one side — there is no one who holds invalid, for in the Gemara the Gemara compares a crack of etrog to a split grain, and in a split grain if it did not crack entirely and a little remains above and a little below it is kosher; and the same with etrog, thus Bach. And to me requires further study, for in the Gemara it compares, etc. — how is it possible to say that per the view that two sides suffice, majority of two sides suffices? For in such a case in a split grain from two sides with a little above and a little below it is also kosher, and there is no difference in grain between one side and two sides. And our version in Ran: at its length in its width from two, etc. — meaning what was in Bach's version "at its majority" and our version instead of the word "on its majority" writes "in its width," and the word "on its majority" was not mentioned at all in Ran:
machatzit-hashekel/17:א: (Seif katan 17) And any change, etc. And to me — if cracked on its pitom, etc. — meaning per the Ran who holds cracked on its pitom even all the more so invalid; even though the reason of a crack being invalid is because of deficiency as Darkei Moshe wrote in this siman, or because of whole taking as implied from Magen Avraham above siman 645 seif katan 16 regarding lulav — nevertheless this that disqualifies on its pitom all the more so requires a reason, for we do not find reasoning to be stringent on its pitom more than another place, except in disqualification that is because of hadar. And as Rashi explained on this that chazazit disqualifies on its pitom all the more so — and these are Rashi's words there: it appears there to the eyes more than other places on it, for at that thickness a person focuses his eyes, end of Rashi's words. And if so, necessarily it must be that this which disqualifies a crack on its pitom all the more so — even though in a crack the reason is not because of hadar, but because of deficiency or we require whole taking — in these invalidations what difference is there between its pitom and another place? Necessarily it must be that in a crack elsewhere nevertheless it is hadar, but in a crack on its pitom its hadar goes away and it is not hadar, therefore it disqualifies all the more so, for there the essence of hadar depends and there the crack is more visible:
machatzit-hashekel/17:ב: (2) And the same law applies to all etrog disqualifications, so too the Ran. Therefore also in this the above reason must apply, even though those etrog disqualifications are not invalid because of hadar — even though they have deficiency, what disqualifies them? Nevertheless it is hadar; but when that disqualification is on its pitom, then its hadar is gone and invalid all seven:
machatzit-hashekel/17:ג: (3) And requires further study on Rabbi Yitzchak, etc. — since he wrote in his book that a crack disqualifies (meaning all the more so), etc., and all the more so dry, etc.; and the words of Magen Avraham require explanation in seif 5 he wrote in the name of "there are those who say" to disqualify a crack all the more so on its pitom; and it teaches us here regarding dry that even per one who permits a crack on its pitom all the more so, nevertheless dry on its pitom all the more so he concedes invalid; and so is explicitly in Eliyah Rabbah; and even though also regarding dry he wrote the language "there are those who say" — nevertheless the intent is thus that dry is stricter than a crack. And in my humble opinion one can say the intent of Magen Avraham is that in the Gemara it is not explained explicitly the law of pitom except regarding chazazit that disqualifies on its pitom all the more so; and the Rosh innovated: since chazazit is invalid because of hadar, so too all invalidations because of hadar disqualify on its pitom all the more so; but what is invalid because of something else, not because of hadar — also on its pitom requires the measure to disqualify like in another place:
machatzit-hashekel/17:ד: (4) And the Ran added that even a crack disqualifies on its pitom all the more so. That is, in a crack elsewhere still hadar remains; nevertheless when cracked on its pitom it is not hadar and disqualifies all the more so. And the same for all disqualifications — whatever the reason of disqualification may be; nevertheless if that disqualification is on its pitom, its beauty goes away and disqualifies all the more so. If so, since all concede what is invalid because of hadar disqualifies on its pitom all the more so — and the chazazit stated in the Gemara that disqualifies on its pitom all the more so is not specifically; rather on this the Rosh and Ran disagree regarding crack and the like that are not invalid because of hadar — if that disqualification is on its pitom whether it still has hadar or not: per the Ran there is no hadar, and per the Rosh it still has hadar; therefore it is difficult for Magen Avraham, since he wrote in seif 5 in the name of "there are those who say" that a crack disqualifies on its pitom all the more so — and this is from the Ran's reason that there is no hadar; in any case it is proven that whatever is not hadar disqualifies on its pitom all the more so, and chazazit that disqualifies on its pitom all the more so is not specifically; and automatically we hear that whatever is invalid elsewhere because of hadar is certainly for all disqualifying on its pitom all the more so; and if so, what is written here regarding dry that "there are those who say" it disqualifies on its pitom all the more so — it is an obvious matter and invalid for all, for dry is certainly invalid because of hadar and all concede it disqualifies on its pitom all the more so; and we know this from what Magen Avraham wrote in seif 5 that here for all it is invalid, since we already heard from seif 5 that the chazazit the Gemara mentioned is not specifically:
machatzit-hashekel/22:א: (Seif katan 22) Pickled in vinegar, etc. In vinegar, even if it did not stay except enough to boil, it is like cooked. See siman 473 seif katan 14 and siman 497 seif katan 3; and in Sefer Eliyah Rabbah he wrote: and requires further study, for Shach and Peri Chadash in Yoreh De'ah end of siman 105 concluded that even in vinegar requires from time to time, and so held the Tur, etc., end of his words. And in my humble opinion it escaped me the words of Magen Avraham in siman 647 seif katan 28 that he wrote: and therefore if it stood in a vinegar vessel, etc., enough that they put water on it and it boils — forbidden by law as written in Yoreh De'ah siman 105; and even though Shach wrote there that also in vinegar requires from time to time — one should not be lenient against Shulchan Aruch, for in the Mishnah, etc.; and even though in siman 104 he wrote that also in vinegar requires from time to time — it must be that it deals with vinegar that is not so strong, and so from Rashi and Tosafos there that it deals with beer vinegar; and the same with wine vinegar that is not so strong, etc., end of Magen Avraham's words. And if so one can say Magen Avraham follows his method that agreed with Shulchan Aruch in Yoreh De'ah siman 105, not like Shach and Peri Chadash; and even though Magen Avraham here wrote anonymously and did not write that it deals specifically with strong wine vinegar — this is a difficulty, for also in Shulchan Aruch Yoreh De'ah siman 105 he wrote anonymously "vinegar"; and nevertheless Magen Avraham explained it deals with strong wine vinegar, for such is the anonymous vinegar the poskim mention in most places:
magen-avraham/9:_: On its majority. From the anonymous wording it is implied that he holds "its majority" means from two sides, as the Tur wrote:
mishnah-berurah/1:א: (1) Dry — and if it is dry only in part of it, see below in seif 12 and in Mishna Berurah there:
mishnah-berurah/2:ה: (10) Even though there is deficiency in them — meaning that it sometimes appears on an etrog that had a hole while still attached, only that skin and flesh grew over it from above — in this there is room to permit; but if we see it was not grown over but there is a hole and deficiency, even though done by thorns in the way of its growth, it is invalid; and this is what he concluded "however if he sees," etc.; and the multitude of people err in this, thinking there is a leniency when the hole was made by thorns:
mishnah-berurah/6:ג: (26) Green as in its creation — and if the peeled place differs in appearance from the appearance of the etrog, even if only its majority was peeled it is invalid; and all this specifically when everything was peeled at once; but if peeled in two and three places, even in a minority of the etrog, if it does not resemble the rest of the etrog it is invalid because it is like speckled; and if peeled at the place of its pitom when the peeled place does not resemble the rest of the etrog, even in any amount it is invalid, and like regarding chazazit below in seif 9; and there are those who say not to be stringent in all this except specifically when the peeled place changed to invalid appearance such as black and white, but if it has kosher appearance one should not disqualify it; and in time of need one may rely on this; and see below in seif 13 in the gloss:
mishnah-berurah/14:ג: (53) And nothing was missing — meaning he did not peel from it except the thin outer peel; if something was missing from it, even in just one place, it is invalid per the first view above in seif 2; and see below siman 649 seif 5 in the gloss and in what we wrote there, in Mishna Berurah seif katan 138:
mishnah-berurah/15:א: (54) Pickled in vinegar — meaning that in this, even if it did not stay except enough to boil, it is like cooked; and the same when soaked in water or other liquids; and honey from time to time — we rule it is like cooked:
peri-megadim/3:_: If — Taz, see in letter 1, and it depends on explaining the sugya 36:1 whether it refers to 2 or to the first clause or the latter clause, and in explaining the Mishnah. And per this, in the first view mefulesh without any deficiency is invalid, and not mefulesh — any hole like issur-size; and without deficiency a wide nail is invalid; but deficient all the more so from flesh and thick etrog peel as below in Taz letter 10 invalid on first day of Yom Tov as below 649 likewise in the gloss, and there it will be explained if so. And the second view is lenient that whatever has no deficiency at all does not disqualify even mefulesh; and whatever has deficiency — mefulesh deficient all the more so invalid; and not mefulesh like issur-size deficiency — behold without deficiency even like issur-size does not disqualify; and so in Hagahot HaRosh zatzal chapter 8 paragraph 6 that always requires deficiency specifically; and Rabbenu Yerucham who wrote in time of need per the second view to declare kosher that not mefulesh deficient all the more so — it is implied that mefulesh without deficiency, or not mefulesh and no deficiency and there is issur-size — even in time of need invalid; and three dispute the two views:
peri-megadim/6:_: That it was pierced — Taz, see in letter 1 from side to side not facing the chambers — not mefulesh does not contradict here, because it deals with a place where there is a thick partition between the chambers, then it is mefulesh. And Tosafos Sukkah 34a s.v. "if it was pierced," and in Rosh there he brought the view in BeHag — it is the first view here. And for practical halacha requires further study, for in Beit Yosef it is implied that Rif and Rambam omitted the Yerushalmi question and mefulesh from side to side specifically; and if so it is implied the halacha is per the author's general rule. And what Taz wrote on Bach that wanted to explain three disputes, and per Ran only the outer peel until the flesh of the etrog is also called mefulesh; and Taz explained Ran wrote until the seed chambers. And what he wrote from terumah, etc., gizzard — see in Pri Megadim Yoreh De'ah siman 49 that very thin outer skin — nevertheless with all the flesh it is included in one skin; and skin two is the whiteness inside hard stuck to flesh — mefulesh hole treifah even though a pocket in which food that peeled by itself; and in chicken placed independently was not included; see there. And there this was explained. And see letter 10 in Taz from this. And what he wrote in paragraph 1 of terumah "they throw away pierced vegetables" — Taz zatzal holds it refers also to etrog peel; see there. And see if so in letters 7 and 10; see there:
peri-megadim/14:_: In two — or Taz, still I do not know the measure of distance in two how much until it is speckled; and to say width of straw we require — I did not find this explicit. And see in Pri Megadim chapter 8 paragraph 17 from lulav he expanded and brought many places. And see in Sefer Kefut Tamarim. And the word "rose on it" chazazit 34 in detached (as rose on it a palm branch) — the same in attached except we require they be higher than the rest of the etrog; see there; and if so in Magen Avraham 19 it will be explained:
peri-megadim/18:_: Unless — Taz, Bach disqualifies green appearance (green) in part, for we require hadar and its law is like chazazit; see there; but Taz zatzal holds in the conclusion the reason is not because of hadar, and therefore R' Meir permits and R' Yehuda disqualifies because its fruit did not finish; and it is implied green like field grasses siman 34 its fruit — even if one leaves it and it greens; and that which is not like field grasses siman that should return to etrog appearance. And if part of it is like egg yolk etrog appearance — possible also part like field grasses is kosher; requires further study in all this (and one should have hadar after a beautiful etrog, and hadar if possible; and in Magen Avraham it will be explained further):
peri-megadim/19:_: That still — Taz, the word "since" requires further study, and it is implied whatever is not like an egg — even if it remains thus unripe is called and not fruit; behold like an egg even if left on the tree it will grow many times more — still found now unripe is called; nevertheless it is fruit even now and fit to emend apparently, even though in the end it will be bigger — instead of "since"; and see Levush; requires further study now; and if so in Magen Avraham letter 24 it will be explained further. If shriveled less than an egg — invalid; see Magen Avraham 649:27; requires further study, for egg — the reason is its fruit did not finish; see Levush, and behold its fruit finished; and to say we require hadar — this too requires further study; understand, and see Magen Avraham here and 649 in Taz and Magen Avraham if so it will be explained further:
shaarei-teshuvah/1:_: Dry. Abir HaTur, and see in Magen Avraham in the name of Shulchan Aruch HaGedolah: chazazit that rises detached is only because of dryness and shriveled and kosher; and therefore partial shriveled is kosher; and see below seif katan 17 that he wrote that one can say in Shulchan Aruch, and there are those who say dry likewise — meaning to exclude from Shulchan Aruch HaGedolah; see there; and see in Peri Megadim there and in seif katan 19 he wrote that the conclusion of all poskim implies that even chazazit that rose detached disqualifies; see there:
shaarei-teshuvah/10:_: In Shulchan Aruch "peeled," etc. And see what I wrote in responsa Beit Ephraim siman 60 where I explained this matter of peeled beautifully, and there I brought from responsa Beit Yaakov siman 87; and see there what he wrote that the words of Shulchan Aruch that wrote "and there are those who say" we require a remainder like a sela — requires further study; see there:
shaarei-teshuvah/15:_: Covered. Abir HaTur, and in responsa Shulchan Aruch HaRav part 1 siman 35 he challenged Beit Yaakov and wrote it is against the implication of the Gemara, and wherever we require by Torah law whole and complete taking — whatever is not attached in its growth, attachment through something else certainly is not attachment to be called whole and complete; and he rejected the proofs of Beit Yaakov from Eruvin daf 81 and from Sukkah daf 36; see there; and also Eliyah Rabbah disagrees with him; see there; and see in Peri Megadim that if its wood is in a fiber and inside the wood a hollow reaches into the etrog, as is sometimes found in a deed — invalid:
shaarei-teshuvah/16:_: In Shulchan Aruch "and its pitom, meaning from the place," etc. And see in Beit Yosef that he brought Rashi's language who wrote "and on its pitom in the thickness of its height that slopes from there," etc.; and he also brought the Rosh's language, and at the end of his words wrote all versions in explanation of the Rosh's words; and so the common word — if the custom is also in the thickness of its height itself to disqualify, or the custom is specifically from the thickness of its height and above, and the thickness of its height is not included; see there; and in Shulchan Aruch's language that wrote "from the place it begins," etc., and so below seif 12 "from the place it begins to slope," etc. — somewhat implied the latter wording is primary that the thickness of its height is not included, even though Bach wrote in the name of his teacher the rabbi zatzal that the thickness of its height is included in the disqualification to disqualify chazazit all the more so; see there — perhaps also in Shulchan Aruch what he wrote "from the place it begins," etc., and also the place is included, since anonymously we recite stringently, and somewhat reasonable thus; and follow the reason that on its pitom it appears more to the eyes, and if so on the thickness of its height also it is no worse than the slope where also it appears clearly to the eyes; and nevertheless in time of need one may be lenient on the other days:
turei-zahav/1:א: By passing a needle through it. So too the Rosh and Tur; and it is difficult — for perhaps there will be a mefulesh hole in it, and it is invalid per the Rosh and Tur, and likewise in Shulchan Aruch seif 2 per the first view; one can say that mefulesh does not disqualify except when pierced from this side to the opposite side facing it or to the seed chambers; but if the hole on one side is mefulesh, that is, through its thickness, certainly all agree it does not disqualify without deficiency, for we derive etrog laws from treifot of an animal, and in treifot if there is a mefulesh hole in the thickness of the limb such as in the heart or intestines and it does not reach the cavity, certainly there is no treifah; so too here with etrog:
turei-zahav/2:ב: Even though there is deficiency in them — this is their way of growth. He derives it in Terumat HaDeshen from treifot of a lung: if there is a lung missing that has a wrinkle and crack — if it rises in swelling and skin and flesh remain, it is kosher; and such is the case with an etrog that while growing had skin and flesh remain — kosher; but whatever will be missing from it after it was detached — impossible that its skin and body remain, end of his words; it is clear his intent: we see the etrog's skin grew over in that missing place, only there is deficiency and a hollow there — in this he permitted; but if we see it was not grown over but there is a hole and deficiency, even though done by thorns in the way of its growth, it is invalid; and this is what he concluded "however if he sees," etc. And these thorns do not raise or lower regarding a hole — only he mentioned them in Terumat HaDeshen because then it is common that there the hole's skin remains intact; and the multitude err in this, thinking there is a leniency when the hole was made by thorns:
turei-zahav/7:ב: And there are those stringent that if the blossom was removed, etc. There is no explicit view on this, only that the Rif wrote: explanation of its pitom — the bud of the etrog, and it is its pitom as we learned "the bud of a pomegranate," and it is the blossom, end of his words; and Ran wrote: per the Rif the pitom was the blossom itself; and it appears to me, etc.; and Beit Yosef wrote that also per the Rif the disqualification is on the bud itself and not on the blossom, for it says "bud" and it is the pitom, and the blossom is not called a bud but pitom — therefore; and that which the Rif said "and it is its blossom" — explanation: the bud itself is called its blossom since it has a blossom, it is called by its name; and so one can explain the Tur's language that wrote "its pitom was removed" — and it is the flower on its head, etc. — meaning the bud itself is called thus because of the flower on the head of the bud; and so from his language in hints that wrote "its pitom was removed — invalid, and it is the flower on its head that protrudes from the head of the etrog," etc.; and if on the flower itself that is the blossom he should not have said "protrudes from the head of the etrog" but should have said "protrudes from the head of the bud"; but certainly he speaks of the bud itself and called it flower; and in my humble opinion: if we have before us an etrog mehudar in the rest of its qualities only that it lacks the blossom, or part of the bud above was removed, and another etrog that is not mehudar in the rest of its qualities only that it has a blossom — one should not pay attention to that blossom; and all the more so where there is doubt whether it had a blossom at all, since Ran, Maggid, and Beit Yosef in the name of Orach Chayyim wrote thus — it is fit to rule practical halacha; and certainly one may rely on them for practical halacha:
turei-zahav/8:_: That the entire width of the hollow is covered. Explanation: in the hollow there some of the wood remains as it was at first:
turei-zahav/9:_: In two or in three places. In several places he wrote: and these are his words — it was always difficult for me, whether in the Gemara or in the poskim: now two invalid, three uncertain — and I did not find any author anything on this; requires further study, end of his words. And in my humble opinion: it is an example of what we say in general — if testimony is established with two, why does Scripture specify three? Rather it compares three to two, etc.; so too here it is certain: if there are two chazazit adjacent to each other but there is some etrog appearance between them like a hair's breadth — we do not say it should be invalid, because for this reason it does not appear speckled; rather there must be some measure between them — and this is if there are 3 chazazit per the measure that is between the two outer ones from one to the other, where the middle chazazit is; so too if there are two alone and between them empty space of this measure, then it appears speckled; as seems to me, correct:
turei-zahav/21:_: Unless it returns to appearance, etc. It appears the explanation: even while still green it is kosher, since it can return to etrog appearance — for he told him it is not kosher except after it becomes like etrog appearance; this is obvious it is kosher, and what does it teach us? And are not all etrogs in the world green at first? And so is Tosafos' language that wrote: and those etrogs that come before us are green like a citron even per R' Yehuda when they return to the appearance of other etrogs, even detached, after staying in a vessel a long time — for certainly their fruit finished, end of his words; and if one thought it is not kosher except after returning to kosher appearance — what is the greatness of a long time, since it returned hadar? Rather certainly the kosher status is immediately even while green, since in the end they will return to etrog appearance even for a long time; and in the Gemara they ask: and R' Yehuda does not require hadar? And we learned: green like a citron — R' Meir permits and R' Yehuda disqualifies — not because he requires hadar, not because the fruit did not finish; and at first glance we should have said: since in the Gemara it only asks on R' Yehuda who does not require hadar, and on this the reason is explained because the fruit did not finish — automatically for us who rule we require hadar, invalid because it lacks hadar; and per this, even if afterward it returns to etrog appearance — invalid because now it is not hadar, unless it already returned; this is not so, for Ran already wrote in the mishnah at the beginning of the chapter that Scripture did not specify anything but anonymously said this mitzvah should be mehudar and transmitted to the Sages, etc., end of his words; therefore per the questioner's reasoning here that the reason in green is invalid per R' Yehuda is because of hadar — meaning we grasp that green is not hadar; but per the answerers that the reason is because fruit did not finish — then we have no proof to say green is not hadar; automatically we should not disqualify it as long as we have finished fruit; and proof for this that Tosafos concluded that certainly the fruit finished and they did not mention this is hadar; but certainly now we are not concerned for green shade because of hadar at all, since we do not find the Sages were concerned for this because of hadar but because fruit did not finish; and therefore permitted even while green since there is finished fruit; and with this the language of Tur that wrote "but if while leaving it," etc., is reconciled for me; and Beit Yosef wrote this wording is not precise, rather it should have been written thus; and that which is invalid means even while leaving it, etc.; and I say he well precisioned: for if he had written per Beit Yosef's language it would be that it is not kosher except after it returned; therefore he wrote "but if it is green" — meaning even while still green it is kosher since it can return afterward; and he did not disqualify it except like field grasses that remain green forever; so it appears to me clear and simple; and I saw Mohach zatzal explained the matters that it is not kosher except after all of it becomes etrog appearance, and he was not precise in this; and in Maharil he wrote it is forbidden to buy green ones unless it already began partially toward etrog appearance, lest it remain green:
yad-ephraim/1:_: In Taz seif katan 5 — but in doubt kosher, etc.; see in Darkei Moshe who wrote that it is implied from his words that in these piercings it is usual that skin and flesh remain intact unless we see they are not intact, end of his words. And requires further study on Taz who led Rama's view to another matter — and if it were visible to Darkei Moshe he would not have written thus:
yad-ephraim/4:_: Taz seif katan 19 — to be bigger as it should be, and meaning that it will grow more like a tree and its fruit will finish; therefore even now it is considered fruit; and this is explained in the words of the Rosh who wrote: and the Rabbis who permit unripe concede regarding less than an egg that it is invalid, for unripe is more than an egg and in the end will finish and is considered fruit; and the words of Shulchan Aruch here are taken from the Tur's words which are from these words of the Rosh. And since I saw emend in Taz "even though in the end it will be bigger" — in truth that is not Taz's intent regarding size measure, only regarding growing from the tree that it will be finished; therefore even though it is still unripe he considers it fruit; and the examiner will see his intent is per the Rosh's words as written; and see in Beit Yosef what he wrote on the words of Semag in this:
